Hindcast forecasts from many origins

Source: R/hindcast.R
pdm_hindcast.Rd

Reruns past forecasts. From each forecast origin the model forecasts the next horizon_h hours, using the rain that actually fell as the forecast rain, so the scores measure the model and its updating, not a rainfall forecast. A forecast LSTM can be given the same origins and scored by the same hindcast_scores().

Usage

pdm_hindcast(
  model,
  forcing,
  observed,
  state = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  every_h = 6,
  horizon_h = 48,
  ar = NULL,
  response_flow = NULL,
  fit_window = NULL,
  state_correction = NULL,
  lower_limit = 0
)

Arguments

model

A FlodePdmModel.

forcing

Data frame with rain and pet, mm per step; optional time.

observed

Observed flow in m3/s, aligned with forcing; NA where missing.

state

Starting state; by default steady state at the first observed flow.

window

Row numbers in which forecast origins may lie, typically the validation or test window. Default: every row after the first 10 per cent.

every_h

Hours between forecast origins.

horizon_h

Forecast horizon in hours.

ar

Named list of AR coefficient vectors, Deltares convention. NULL gives the default pair described above; list() gives none.

response_flow

Reference flow in m3/s for the response time. Default: the 90th percentile of observed flow, a typical high flow.

fit_window

Optional row numbers on which to fit AR(3) coefficients, method fitted.

state_correction

NULL for none, or a state_updater() to add method state.

lower_limit

Lowest allowed updated flow, m3/s.

Value

A list: forecasts, a data.table with origin (row), time (if forcing has one), lead (steps), lead_h, method, forecast and observed; ar, the coefficient sets used; response_time, the pdm_response_time() result; and dt.

Details

Methods. Every hindcast includes:

MethodForecast
noneThe simulation, without updating
persistenceThe last observed flow, held for every lead: the baseline to beat
each entry of arThe simulation plus the AR projection of recent error, as in IMFS
fittedAs above, with AR(3) coefficients fitted to the errors in fit_window only
stateState correction at the origin (Moore 2007, Eq. 28-30), then run forward

By default ar holds the Environment Agency 2024 default set and a default-family set whose principal decay is the model's own time to peak at response_flow, from pdm_response_time(). The 2024 default is defined for 15-minute steps; on other steps it is still applied, as given, with a message.

Errors are observed minus simulated flow, in m3/s, additive, as in IMFS. The AR projection at an origin needs the last three errors; if any of those observations is missing, that origin has no AR forecast. Updated flows below lower_limit are raised to it.

No leaks. The simulation runs continuously without updating, so the forecast from an origin uses observations up to that origin only. AR coefficients come from outside the scored period: the fixed sets, or fit_window, which should be the calibration window. Fitting on the scored window would let the AR learn the errors it then corrects.

See also

hindcast_scores(), plot_hindcast(), pdm_response_time(), ar_from_response_time()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 24 * 40
forcing <- data.frame(rain = ifelse(runif(n) < 0.06, rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 4), 0), pet = 0.05)
truth <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 40, fc = 1.1)
observed <- run_pdm(truth, forcing, initial_state_from_flow(truth, 2, 0.7))$output$q_m3s
model <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 40)
hc <- pdm_hindcast(model, forcing, observed, window = (24 * 20 + 1):n, horizon_h = 24)
#> The EA 2024 AR default is defined for 15-minute steps; this model uses 1 h steps
head(hindcast_scores(hc))
#>     method lead_h lead_ratio     n       nse        rmse         mae
